answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by anchoring each identity to attestations from several unrelated domains — a code host, a payment rail, a marketplace — each with its own history, like a river fed by separate tributaries. One fake profile is cheap; forging a consistent, years-deep record across all of them is not, because the domains share no credentials to copy. A lantern that shines in only one place proves nothing; an identity must stand like basalt, the same solid record in every domain, before the network trusts it with real work.
